hook: A clear lake in spring, a green, cloudy lake by August: the difference is often a few kilograms of phosphate washed in from lawns, farms and wastewater. Phosphorus is scarce in nature because it never travels through the air. It creeps out of rock, rides in water and on soil, and settles to the bottom of the sea.

options: The nutrient in shortest supply compared with need
The nutrient plants use the most
prereq.why: Adding the limiting nutrient raises growth.

prereq.q: Which process returns nutrients from dead matter to the soil?
prereq.why: Decomposers break down dead matter and release its nutrients.

figure.caption: The phosphorus cycle has no gas phase: rock, soil, living things, water and sediment.

chain.cause: Plants take up phosphate and animals eat plants
chain.effect: decomposers return phosphate to the soil when they die

chain.cause: Rain washes phosphate-carrying soil into water
chain.effect: it settles as sediment and returns to land only when rock is uplifted, over millions of years

ideas: The main reservoirs are rock and ocean sediments; the phosphorus cycle has no significant gas phase, so it is slow.
Weathering releases phosphate; plants take it up; decomposers return it; sedimentation stores it.
Phosphorus builds DNA, ATP, cell membranes, bones and teeth.
Phosphate is often the limiting nutrient in fresh water, so extra phosphate (fertilizer, detergents, wastewater) makes algae grow fast.

misconception.wrong: Phosphorus cycles through the air like carbon and nitrogen.
misconception.right: Phosphorus has no significant gas form. It moves in rock, soil, water and living things, which is why it cycles slowly and is so often in short supply.

summary: Phosphorus is stored mostly in rock and ocean sediments and has no significant gas phase, so it cycles slowly. Weathering releases phosphate, plants take it up, animals eat plants, and decomposers return it to the soil. Rain carries phosphate on soil into water, where it settles as sediment. Phosphorus often limits growth in fresh water, so extra phosphate makes algae grow.
